title: BHU students protest over women's safety and hostel curfews

tea.why: Students say campus safety arrangements are poor and that restrictions such as a 10 pm curfew fall on women students.
tea.want: Change the women's hostel curfew, improve campus safety (streetlights, roads) and hold the administration accountable.
tea.changed: Oct 4: on the 12th day of their strike, ABVP members and women students wrote protest letters in blood.

summary: Students at Banaras Hindu University in Varanasi have held several protests over campus safety and the rules applied to women students. Groups have held candlelight and torchlight marches and asked the university to change the 10 pm curfew in women's hostels, fix streetlights and roads, and improve administrative accountability. The BHU unit of the ABVP has been on an indefinite strike over a 10-point charter of demands; on October 4, the 12th day, its members and women students wrote letters in their blood to the administration. AISA, Disha and BSM held a separate joint protest.
organizers: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) BHU unit
demands: Change the 10 pm curfew in women's hostels
Better campus safety, lighting and roads
response: No response from the university administration is reported in the sources; protesters describe the administration as indifferent.

updates.text: Students held candlelight and torchlight marches over women's safety and hostel curfews.
ABVP's indefinite strike reached day 12; members wrote protest letters in blood.

UP: ABVP workers, female students write letters with blood; protest over administration's indifference
